dataSource.fetchedBy: research agent, verified against the official source
dataSource.notes:
SOURCING. Every number comes from Starbucks' own US menu system at starbucks.com/menu. The public menu pages are a JS SPA, so I read the same JSON the site itself renders from: the category tree at https://www.starbucks.com/apiproxy/v1/ordering/menu and per-item detail at https://www.starbucks.com/apiproxy/v1/ordering/{productNumber}/{formCode} (same payload behind each item's "Full nutrition & ingredients" page, e.g. https://www.starbucks.com/menu/product/407/hot/nutrition). I confirmed by rendering that nutrition page in a browser and matching the on-page values (Orange Cream Cold Brew Grande: 240 cal / 2g protein / 28g carb / 14g fat) to the API payload field-for-field.

METHOD. Pulled all 284 in-store products (306 total minus At Home Coffee whole bean / VIA), giving 801 size-level nutrition rows with zero missing macros. Calories come from nutrition.calories; protein/carbs/fat from nutrition.additionalFacts ids protein / totalCarbs / totalFat. Serving weights come from nutrition.servingSize. The final menu was generated programmatically from that extract — no hand-typed numbers — then verified two ways: (1) 14 hand-picked items re-checked directly against the raw per-product JSON files, all 14 exact; (2) a global check that every one of the 161 emitted (cal, protein, carb, fat) tuples matches a real source row exactly. 161 unique slugs, no collisions, no negative values.

NOTHING WAS REVERSE-ENGINEERED. Starbucks publishes per-item line values, so all macros are as-published for exactly the serving named. No combo was decomposed and no value was derived or estimated.

PORTION BASIS. Beverages are Grande (16 fl oz), Starbucks' standard size, on the standard recipe (default milk and default syrup pumps for that drink). Exceptions where Grande does not exist and the source's own default size is used instead: Cortado is Short (8 fl oz), Espresso and Iced Espresso are Doppio (1.5 fl oz). Food is one item at the weight Starbucks states; "1 item (42 g)" for Rolled & Steel-Cut Oatmeal is the dry oat portion as the source lists it, not the prepared weight. Bottled items are the whole container. Starbucks' own disclaimer applies: values are for the standard recipe and customization changes them.

CATEGORY IDS. Food stations reuse the existing vocabulary (mains, breads, sides, extras) with display names that fit Starbucks. The five drink stations (hot-coffee, cold-coffee, tea, refreshers, frappuccino) are new ids because nothing in the vocabulary honestly describes a beverage station, and the free-add-on portion default is the correct behavior for a drink — a split-base id like proteins or bases would let a latte be halved against another drink, which is wrong. Drink stations are selectOne since a Starbucks order anchors on one beverage.

CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING. Starbucks' edge (Akamai) rate-limits aggressively; it IP-blocked me mid-pull and I had to back off ~10 minutes and refetch at ~1 request per 4s. Anyone re-running this should throttle. Menu snapshot taken 2026-08-07 against the US en-US menu with no store number set, so it reflects the national default menu; individual stores may not carry every item.
